A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Focal-SAM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, domain-generalization, training-time, hyperparameter, and loss-landscape experiments involving ResNet and CLIP models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparisons against SAM trained for additional epochs in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The focal sharpness objective, class weights, perturbation calculation, and three-backpropagation optimization procedure remain unchanged. Equations (4)–(8) and Algorithm 1 specify the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10 LT, CIFAR-100 LT, ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist, and the same ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNetV2, and ImageNet-C evaluations. The added computational-cost comparisons reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added comparisons use existing SAM combinations with longer training budgets, not new comparison methods. Newly cited SSE-SAM is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds an approximate computational-cost control: SAM receives 300 rather than 200 epochs for training from scratch, or 30 rather than 20 for fine-tuning, while Focal-SAM retains its original budgets. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables 8–10 test whether Focal-SAM's advantages persist when SAM receives additional training to approximate comparable computational cost. This focused supplementary analysis covers three existing datasets; the original hyperparameter, corruption, Hessian, and loss-landscape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Existing ablation plots are retained, and new Tables 8–10 report point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are unchanged, but Tables 8–10 add longer-training SAM results that narrow gaps and occasionally reverse rankings. For CIFAR-100 LT IR100 with LDAM+DRW, v1 reports SAM/Focal-SAM accuracies of 49.5/50.3 at 200 epochs; v2 additionally reports 50.4 for 300-epoch SAM against the retained 50.3 for 200-epoch Focal-SAM. These are different-budget results.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 becomes Theorem 4.1, and the proofs move from Appendix B to Appendix A. The mathematical definitions, assumptions, bounds, lemmas, and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient class-specific sharpness control, a sharper generalization bound, and effectiveness for conventional and foundation models. The new control experiment supports existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning head–tail flatness, domain generalization, and hyperparameter tradeoffs remain substantively unchanged. The added computational-cost experiment introduces no new mechanism explanation, applicability boundary, or explicit limitation.

D1.justification: The hardware disclosure expands from RTX 3090 GPUs in v1 Appendix D.5 to RTX 3090 and RTX 4090 GPUs in v2 Appendix C.5. Appendix D.3 also specifies the added training budgets; existing backbone and optimization details are retained. The hardware revision does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds fifteen references within existing related-work categories, including SSE-SAM and several AUC-oriented methods. This expands citation coverage, but the explanations of prior approaches and Focal-SAM's research positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to main-text Section 2, and the training-speed and sharpness subsections exchange order. v2 also adds acknowledgements, updates affiliation and conference text, and makes limited wording edits; most prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–10, exchanges the order and numbering of the two supplementary CIFAR tables, and repositions retained material. Figures 1–11 retain the same graphics; the changes concern additional tables and layout rather than redesigned visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's equal-epoch comparisons, Appendix D.3 provides a useful check against longer-trained SAM. Tables 8–10 retain most overall advantages while revealing exceptions, strengthening the empirical evaluation. The benefit is limited because the blanket 1.5-fold epoch adjustment only approximates the dataset-dependent timing ratios in Table 1, and the new results lack uncertainty estimates.
